After investigating, we found out that another worker process running OpenProject 17.2.x was running on another host and was connected to the same database. Both the 17.5 and the 17.2 workers were processing jobs. The one running 17.5 was running correctly, the one running 17.2 was marking a lot of job as failed discarded because it could not load jobs like `ProjectIdentifiers::ConvertProjectToSemanticIdsJob`. We detected it through the "Processes" tab of the good_job admin interface. We saw the two worker processes running on different machines. Both the 17.5 and the 17.2 workers were processing jobs. The one running 17.5 was running correctly, the one running 17.2 was marking a lot of jobs as failed/discarded because it could not load jobs like `ProjectIdentifiers::ConvertProjectToSemanticIdsJob`. We detected it through the "Processes" tab of the good_job admin interface. We saw the two worker processes running on different machines. It would be helpful to have this "Processes" information somewhere in OpenProject to help with diagnosis. **Acceptance criteria** * The number of worker processes and whether they are all running the latest version is reported somewhere in OpenProject. * It could be in `/health_checks/xxx` endpoints * It could be in Administration > Information page * Or somewhere else. * The information needed to diagnose and upgrade or terminate deviant worker processes is available: * Are all workers up-to-date (if possible to get this information)? * Which version is running (if possible)? * Where is the worker located? **Technical notes** * Active processes can be fetched with `GoodJob::Process.active` * `GoodJob::Process` instances have a `state` with useful information: `process.state.slice("hostname", "pid", "proctitle").inspect` * We can probably extend the state with custom information: ```ruby # config/initializers/good_job_process_version.rb ActiveSupport.on_load(:good_job_process) do # self is GoodJob::Process here singleton_class.prepend(Module.new do def process_state super.merge(openproject_version: OpenProject::VERSION::STRING) end end) end ```

After investigating, we found out that another worker process running OpenProject 17.2.x was running on another host and was connected to the same database. Both the 17.5 and the 17.2 workers were processing jobs. The one running 17.5 was running correctly, the one running 17.2 was marking a lot of job as failed discarded because it could not load jobs like `ProjectIdentifiers::ConvertProjectToSemanticIdsJob`. We detected it through the "Processes" tab of the good_job admin interface. We saw the two worker processes running on different machines. That would be helpful to have this "Processes" information somewhere in OpenProject to help diagnosis. **Acceptance criteria** * The number of workers processes and if they are all running the latest version is reported somewhere in OpenProject. * It could be in /health_checks/xxx endpoints * It could be in Administration > Information page * or somewhere else. * The information needed to diagnose and upgrade or terminate deviant worker processes is available: * are all workers up-to-date (if possible to get this information) * which version is running (if possible) * where is the worker located **Technical notes** * Active processes can be fetched with `GoodJob::Process.active` * `GoodJob::Process` instances have a `state` with useful information: `process.state.slice("hostname", "pid", "proctitle").inspect` * We can probably extend the state with custom information: ```ruby # config/initializers/good_job_process_version.rb ActiveSupport.on_load(:good_job_process) do # self is GoodJob::Process here singleton_class.prepend(Module.new do def process_state super.merge(openproject_version: OpenProject::VERSION::STRING) end end) end ```

response.output: **As a** project team member   **I want to** see sequential numbers on each activity/comment entry in the Activity tab (e.g. #1, #2, #3) **so that** I can easily reference and find specific comments in discussions (e.g. "See comment #12") **Acceptance criteria** * Each activity entry in the Activity tab displays a visible, sequential number starting at #1 * The number increments sequentially per work package (not based on internal journal/version IDs) * The number functions as a clickable permalink/anchor link (e.g. #activity-12) that can be copied and shared * The numbering is consistent regardless of filter settings (show everything / show changes only / show comments only) * When a user clicks an activity permalink, the page scrolls to and highlights the referenced activity * Existing references to old comment numbers (from before v15.0) should resolve correctly again **Technical notes** * The original spec in #54733 listed #id as a required meta element ("Current elements must be present") * Bugs #58513 (numbers were random) and #59157 (number was not a proper link) indicate the previous implementation used internal journal.version rather than a sequential counter — a simple sequential counter per work package would avoid these issues * The mobile app (#61447) explicitly removed enumeration; this feature should be restored in both web and mobile * Consider whether numbering should count all journal entries (changes + comments) or only comments — the old behavior counted all entries **Permissions and visibility considerations** * To whom is this feature visible? On non-working days, there is no reducton as no work is expected to take place. * Story points added/removed after the sprint's start date (e.g. by removing/adding work packages or changing the work packages's story points) do not affect the Guideline-dataset * If the sprint runs longer than anticipated (complete button not pressed after finish date), the Guideline series still points to the planned date as this is what was planned with. * "Remaining story points (projection)" is similar to "Guideline" but starts from the point where "Remaining story points" ends. From there, the data series decreases in a straight line to 0 (only non working days stop the decrease). * This series only exist if the sprint is ongoing (started but not finished). It is also not existing if the current time exceeds the planned end of the sprint. * The non-working days are displayed as a gray bar with lower opacity (see if it's implementable this way) * Chart.js can display specific data points on hover, so the user can see the nubmer at each point the value changes * open: what could we include here? just the number, or also links and IDs to the WPs? * A blankslate is displayed instead of a graph [(mockup link)](https://www.figma.com/design/owpxg3fdqZONIGL6SBSG8M/Agile--Sprint-reports?node-id=2454-19983&t=mOl1xRIFT1sxRayJ-1) * If the sprint doesn't have a start and an end date * If the user has the "create sprint" permission, the blankslate includes the ability to set the date * If the current date is before the sprint's start date * If no work package has had any story point set throughout the sprint's interval * The start/finish dates of the graph are determined as specified by ###AGILE-399 **Permissions and visibility considerations** * If the user is able to see the sprint, the graph is visibel.

On non-working days, there is no reduction as no work is expected to take place. * Story points added/removed after the sprint's start date (e.g. by removing/adding work packages or changing the work packages's story points) do not affect the Guideline-dataset * If the sprint runs longer than anticipated (complete button not pressed after finish date), the Guideline series still points to the planned date as this is what was planned with. * "Remaining story points (projection)" is similar to "Guideline" but starts from the point where "Remaining story points" ends. From there, the data series decreases in a straight line to 0 (only non working days stop the decrease). * This series only exist if the sprint is ongoing (started but not finished). It is also not existing if the current time exceeds the planned end of the sprint. * The non-working days are displayed as a gray bar with lower opacity (see if it's implementable this way) * Chart.js can display specific data points on hover, so the user can see the number at each point the value changes * open: what could we include here? just the number, or also links and IDs to the WPs? * A blankslate is displayed instead of a graph [(mockup link)](https://www.figma.com/design/owpxg3fdqZONIGL6SBSG8M/Agile--Sprint-reports?node-id=2454-19983&t=mOl1xRIFT1sxRayJ-1) * If the sprint doesn't have a start and an end date * If the user has the "create sprint" permission, the blankslate includes the ability to set the date * If the current date is before the sprint's start date * If no work package has had any story point set throughout the sprint's interval * The start/finish dates of the graph are determined as specified by  ###AGILE-399 **Permissions and visibility considerations** * If the user is able to see the sprint, the graph is visible.

ORIGINAL: ### Description: Several employees reported an issue when using checkbox (task) lists inside a table in a work package description. If a checkbox list item has nested sub-items, the parent (top-level) items become invisible after saving the work package. This happens both when: * the sub-items are **checkboxes**, or * the sub-items are **bulleted list items** under a parent checkbox item. * (I haven't tested the issue on numbered list items) In edit mode, the parent items briefly appear when clicking into the description field, but after saving again, the parent checkbox remains without any visible text/description. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open any work package and edit the description. 2. Insert/create a table in the description. 3. Inside a table cell, create a checkbox list (task list). 4. Create nested checkbox sub-items under a parent checkbox item (i.e., a parent item with indented sub-items). 5. Save the work package. ### What is the buggy behavior? * After saving, the parent checkbox list items are no longer visible (their text/description disappears). * The checkbox may still be present, but the description is invisible. * When switching back into edit mode (click into the description), the parent items appear briefly. * After saving again, the parent items disappear again. * In the “code view” of the description, the list elements inside the table appear to be output/rendered incorrectly by OpenProject. ### What is the expected behavior? 1. Parent checkbox list items (and their text) should remain visible after saving. 2.
